algorithm: Parallel TCP connect scan over a loopback target
complexity: O(p) connects over p ports, parallelized across worker threads
data_flow_ascii:
port list -> ThreadPoolExecutor -> socket.create_connection
connect success -> OPEN + latency_ms; OSError -> closed + latency_ms
rows sorted by port -> printed open/closed table
description_sentence: A loopback-only TCP port scanner that reports open/closed state and latency, and refuses any non-loopback target.
failure_note: Connection errors are treated as closed ports, never raised; an invalid port range or a non-loopback target exits with a clear error.

functions.desc: Attempt one TCP connect; return (is_open, latency_ms).
functions.name: scan_port
functions.signature: scan_port(host: str, port: int, timeout: float = 0.5) -> tuple

functions.desc: Scan ports in parallel; return dicts sorted by port number.
functions.name: scan_ports
functions.signature: scan_ports(host: str, ports: list, timeout: float = 0.5, workers: int = 8) -> list

functions.desc: Exit with an error unless the host is a loopback address.
functions.name: check_target

functions.desc: Scan around a dummy listener; exactly one port must be open.
functions.name: run_self_test

functions.desc: Scan an explicit port list on a loopback target and print a table.
functions.name: run_scan
functions.signature: run_scan(host: str, ports: list, timeout: float, workers: int) -> int

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.desc: Self-test by default; explicit scan with --ports.
functions.name: main

label: port scanner
output_shape: Prints an open/closed table with per-port latency in ms, plus a PASS/FAIL self-test verdict in default mode.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that checks which local ports are listening and proves itself with a self-test against a dummy listener.

qa.a: check_target() only allows 127.0.0.1, localhost, and ::1; anything else prints an error and exits with status 2.
qa.q: What stops it from scanning other machines?

qa.a: A throwaway listener is opened on an ephemeral port, the range around it is scanned, and the test passes only if exactly that port is open.
qa.q: How does the self-test guarantee an open port?

qa.a: A thread pool runs up to --workers concurrent connects, so a 100-port scan finishes in roughly one timeout instead of 100.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python using parallel TCP connects, restricted to loopback targets with a self-test that validates scan accuracy.
run_notes: --ports scans an explicit list; --target must stay a loopback address; --timeout and --workers tune the scan.
scaling_note: Connect scanning is the slowest scan type; fine for tens of ports locally, not designed for internet-wide sweeping.
storage_note: No persistence: results are printed to stdout and not stored anywhere.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, concurrent.futures, random, socket, sys, time
tradeoff_note: Full TCP connects are reliable and simple but slower and noisier than SYN half-open scans, which need raw sockets.
